# What crates.io tokens the library redacts, and what it leaves alone.
#
# Every token here is built from the ordered run 0123456789abcdef, which no real
# credential is: the body is that run written twice, which is the thirty-two
# characters either form carries. With the opening in front an API token comes to
# thirty-five characters, and with the Trusted Publishing prefix a token comes to
# thirty-nine.
#
# The two forms are one pattern because neither is published by design, both
# authenticate the same endpoints, and a caller with reason to redact one has the
# same reason for the other.
#
# The cases about a body of one class alone carry no ordered run. A body of
# letters and a body of digits are what say the alphabet holds both, and neither
# can be written from a run that carries the other.

patterns: crates-io-token

# An API token as it is written: the credentials file cargo login stores it in,
# the environment variable CI hands it through, the command line it is passed on
# and the header the API reads it from.

case:     a token in the credentials file
in:       token = "cio0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef"
out:      token = "«crates-io-token»"

case:     a token in an environment assignment
in:       CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN=cio0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN=«crates-io-token»

case:     a token on a cargo login command line
in:       cargo login cio0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      cargo login «crates-io-token»

case:     a token in an authorization header
in:       Authorization: cio0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      Authorization: «crates-io-token»

case:     a token at the end of a sentence
in:       the token is cio0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef.
out:      the token is «crates-io-token».

# The Trusted Publishing form, which is the same body behind a longer prefix: a
# CI job exchanges an OIDC token for one and uses it to publish. Its last
# character stands for the XOR of the thirty-one in front of it, and this pattern
# does not do the arithmetic — the f written here is not the o crates.io would
# have written, and it is redacted all the same.

case:     a token in the response that mints it
in:       {"token":"cio_tp_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef","expires_at":"2026-08-17T00:30:00Z"}
out:      {"token":"«crates-io-token»","expires_at":"2026-08-17T00:30:00Z"}

case:     a token in a workflow output
in:       token: cio_tp_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      token: «crates-io-token»

case:     a token whose last character is not the checksum of the rest
in:       cio_tp_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      «crates-io-token»

case:     the same body with the checksum crates.io would write
in:       cio_tp_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdeo
out:      «crates-io-token»

# The body: the letters of both cases and the digits throughout, and the counts
# read exactly rather than as floors. A run longer than the count is a token and
# what was written after it.

case:     an uppercase body
in:       cio0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF
out:      «crates-io-token»

case:     a body of letters alone
in:       cioabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzabcdef
out:      «crates-io-token»

case:     a body of digits alone
in:       cio01234567890123456789012345678901
out:      «crates-io-token»

case:     a body run one character longer is a token and the character after it
in:       cio0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0
out:      «crates-io-token»0

case:     a body one character short is not a token
in:       cio0123456789abcdef0123456789abcde
out:      cio0123456789abcdef0123456789abcde

case:     a hyphen in the body
in:       cio0123456789abcdef-123456789abcdef
out:      cio0123456789abcdef-123456789abcdef

case:     an underscore in the body
in:       cio0123456789abcdef_123456789abcdef
out:      cio0123456789abcdef_123456789abcdef

case:     a dot in the body
in:       cio0123456789abcdef.123456789abcdef
out:      cio0123456789abcdef.123456789abcdef

# What a token may be written against: no boundary on either side of the
# opening, so a token keeps its span whatever character it abuts and what stands
# past its last character stays where it was written.

case:     a token after an underscore
in:       CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN_cio0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN_«crates-io-token»

case:     a token after a letter
in:       xcio0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      x«crates-io-token»

case:     a word written against a token
in:       cio0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdefsuffix
out:      «crates-io-token»suffix

# Tokens written together, and the token written inside another. The alphabet a
# body is drawn from holds every character of the opening, so a body may spell it
# and open a candidate that reads on past the end of the token it stands in. That
# is why the scan resumes a byte past the start of a candidate rather than past
# the candidate, and the last two cases are what a scan stepping over what it
# found would lose: the spans overlap and are redacted as one.

case:     two tokens with nothing between them
in:       cio0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdefcio0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      «crates-io-token»«crates-io-token»

case:     two tokens separated by a space
in:       cio0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef cio0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      «crates-io-token» «crates-io-token»

case:     the two forms written together
in:       cio0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef cio_tp_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      «crates-io-token» «crates-io-token»

case:     an opening in front of a token
in:       ciocio0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      «crates-io-token»

case:     a token beginning inside a Trusted Publishing token
in:       cio_tp_0123456789abcdef0123456cio0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      «crates-io-token»

# And what this pattern leaves alone. First the opening: the case crates.io
# writes it in, and the infix of the longer form written short, hyphenated and
# left out. Then a body of the right length with no opening in front of it, which
# is the shape crates.io issued before the prefix existed and the shape of every
# identifier and content hash besides — its own parser rejects a token carrying
# no prefix, so nothing is left there to read. Then the prose, the log line and
# the line cargo writes, which no pattern here has anything to find in.

case:     an uppercase opening
in:       CIO0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      CIO0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

case:     the Trusted Publishing infix without its closing underscore
in:       cio_tp0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      cio_tp0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

case:     a hyphen where the infix opens
in:       cio-tp-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      cio-tp-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

case:     an underscore behind the opening that begins no infix
in:       cio_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      cio_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

case:     a body of the right length with no opening
in:       0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

case:     a body of the right length behind another word
in:       token=0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      token=0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

case:     a SHA-256 digest
in:       0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

case:     prose
in:       there is no credential in this sentence
out:      there is no credential in this sentence

case:     a log line
in:       time=2026-08-17T00:00:00Z level=info msg="calling api" url=https://crates.io/api/v1/crates
out:      time=2026-08-17T00:00:00Z level=info msg="calling api" url=https://crates.io/api/v1/crates

case:     the line cargo writes while publishing
in:       Uploading my-crate v0.1.0 (/home/runner/work/my-crate/my-crate)
out:      Uploading my-crate v0.1.0 (/home/runner/work/my-crate/my-crate)
